entries.name: Invoice Generator
entries.description: Generate an invoice (PDF/structured) from line items and customer details.

usage.callShape: POST https://orbisapi.com/proxy/invoice-generator-api-e020f1 with JSON body {from, to, number, currency, items:[{name, quantity, unit_cost}]} (slug UNCONFIRMED — see quirks)
usage.outputShape: unknown (never paid; expected PDF bytes or structured invoice JSON per description "Generate an invoice (PDF/structured)")
quirks: BLOCKING: URL slug mismatch between sources. Task brief says slug 2e3f1d; registry spec (qa-batch-current.json) says slug e020f1. For an Orbis proxy the slug IS the route — paying the wrong one loses money to a 404.
Auto-mode money classifier DENIED the payment specifically because the spec slug (e020f1) differs from the brief slug (2e3f1d) and could not be cross-verified.
Orbis proxy: known charge-then-404 pattern. The 402 pre-flight (probe payable:true) does NOT prove the route works.
inputSchema is empty {} — body shape was inferred from the service name + description; field names (from/to/number/currency/items[].unit_cost) are unconfirmed.
Never paid — endpoint untested. Resolve canonical slug, then pay exactly once.
usage.guide: Do not call until the canonical Orbis slug is confirmed: the QA task brief and the registry spec disagree (2e3f1d vs e020f1) and for an Orbis proxy the slug is the route, so a wrong slug charges you and returns 404. Once the correct slug is known, POST a JSON invoice body like {from, to, number, currency, items:[{name, quantity, unit_cost}]} (the input schema is empty so these field names are a best-guess from the service description and may need adjustment on a 422). Pay exactly once — Orbis has a charge-then-404 pattern, so if the post-payment response is 404/HTML/refund, treat the endpoint as broken and stop. Expect either PDF invoice bytes or a structured invoice JSON in the response body.

entries.name: Strale Invoice Validator
entries.description: Validate an invoice's structure, totals, and required fields, returning issues found — billed $0.0216 per call via x402.

usage.outputShape: body.valid (bool), body.errors[] ({field,issue} required-field failures), body.warnings[] ({field,issue} recommended/EU-compliance gaps), body.tax_calculation_check {expected_tax,actual_tax,difference,pass}, body.line_items_check {total_checked,passed,failed}, body.eu_compliant (bool)
quirks: inputSchema is null in the registry; wrap the invoice under an 'invoice' key. The validator's canonical required fields are: invoice_date, vendor_name, vendor_vat, vendor_address, amounts (object with subtotal/tax/total). Recommended (warning-only) fields: buyer_name, buyer_vat, buyer_address, due_date. Each line item should include line_total or it cannot verify line math.

Sending unknown/extra field names does NOT error the call (HTTP 200 always for a well-formed JSON body); the validator simply reports missing required fields as errors. So a wrong field name yields valid:false rather than a 4xx.
body.valid:false is a normal successful response indicating the invoice has issues, not an endpoint failure.
usage.guide: POST a JSON body to https://api.strale.io/x402/invoice-validate with an "invoice" object containing the invoice fields. The canonical fields the validator checks are invoice_date, vendor_name, vendor_vat, vendor_address, an amounts object {subtotal,tax,total}, and line_items[] each with a line_total. Pay $0.0216 USDC on Base via x402 (no API key, no sign-in). Read body.valid for the pass/fail verdict, body.errors[] for blocking required-field problems, body.warnings[] for EU-compliance recommendations, and tax_calculation_check / line_items_check for math validation. A valid:false response is still a successful call.
